steps.title: The names you'll hear
steps.body: Fans and broadcasters measure every new star against a few ==all-time greats==. Know them and half the arguments at the watch party make sense.

steps.title: Tom Brady · QB
steps.body: Won ==7 championships== over 23 seasons, six in New England and one in Tampa Bay. That's ==more than any single team== has won.
steps.note: You'll hear him called the GOAT: greatest of all time.

steps.title: Jerry Rice · WR
steps.body: Holds the career records for ==receiving yards and touchdown catches==, mostly in San Francisco. Many think no one will ever catch him.

steps.title: Lawrence Taylor · LB
steps.body: Rushed the passer so well for New York in the '80s that teams started ==paying left tackles== big money, just to protect the QB's ==blind side==.
steps.note: That story is the heart of the book and movie The Blind Side.

steps.title: Walter Payton · RB
steps.body: Chicago's "Sweetness" ran with grace and punished tacklers. The league's top ==award for community service== is named after him.

steps.title: Know the nicknames
steps.body: Legends go by nicknames: ==Prime Time== (Deion Sanders, who also played pro baseball), ==Beast Mode== (Marshawn Lynch), ==Megatron== (Calvin Johnson) and Sweetness.

steps.prompt: He came off the blind side. Who should have blocked him?
steps.explain: He came from the QB's left, the side a right-handed passer can't see. Protecting that blind side is the left tackle's job.

steps.prompt: Who has won the most championships of any player?
steps.explain: Tom Brady won 7. Joe Montana won 4, Peyton Manning 2. Jerry Rice won 3 as a receiver.
